newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan oil monopoly confirms Crescent talks.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan oil monopoly confirms Crescent talks.

text.p: Taiwan's oil monopoly confirmed on Tuesday it was negotiating an equity acquisition with a United Arab Emirates oil firm, but denied a report that it had offered US$80 million for the deal. State-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp said it was in talks with Crescent Petroleum Company International Ltd of the United Arab Emirates to buy a 40 percent stake in Crescent subsidiary Buttes Gas and Oil.

"Yes, we are continuing the negotiations with Crescent, but we have not discussed prices," said an official, who asked not to be identified. Chinese Petroleum expected a result by the end of February, the official said.
Taiwan's economics ministry, which oversees the monopoly, reported the talks on Monday, saying Taiwan wanted to reduce crude import costs by gaining control over crude sources.
The state-funded Central News Agency has said Chinese Petroleum offered $80 million to secure the 40 percent stake in the private Sharjah oil firm.

Crescent on Monday responded cautiously to the reports, saying only that it was in talks with several foreign firms, including the Taiwan monopoly, on strategic alliances and the possible sale of a minority equity stake in the firm.
Chinese Petroleum said the economics ministry had put it in an awkward position by disclosing the talks.
"The negotiation was supposed to be kept secret because we have signed a non-disclosure agreement with Crescent," the Chinese Petroleum official said.
"Crescent has protested at our violation of the non-disclosure agreement," the official added.
He would not say whether the leak had jeopardised the deal.
Crescent has oil- and gas-producing assets in the Gulf, interests in a Pakistan refinery project and a planned project to transport and sell gas from Qatar to Pakistan.
